Historical basis for the naming and narrative: the Jing-Zhang Railway Works Photographic Record (compiled 1909, Tan Jintang), selected into the China Documentary Heritage program in 2002. Cultural narrative only; not a planning or engineering basis.

Publicly available reference 'Illustrated Century of the Jing-Zhang Railway' (Jin Jing & Bai Hongye, Wenjin Publishing, 2023) and National Library of China map-collection materials on the railway's surveying and photographic archive. Cultural narrative only.

Beijing News article (2023-05-10) on the Jing-Zhang Railway map and the transition from traditional to modern surveying in China; used for the Zhan Tianyou surveying narrative. Cultural narrative only.

Publicly available biography of Zhan Tianyou (1861-1919): Yale-trained engineer, chief engineer of the Jing-Zhang Railway (1905-1909), pioneer of Chinese independent railway construction. Cultural narrative only.

The Doctrine of the Mean, ch. 20 ('study broadly, question carefully, think carefully, distinguish clearly, act resolutely') and ch. 26 ('being broad and thick, it can carry all things'): methodology and naming basis. Classical quotation only, not a planning basis.
The Analects, Yang Huo chapter ('Are there not games of chess?') and other chapters: naming basis for the Gameplay (Boyi) pillar. Classical quotation only, not a planning basis.

The Book of Rites, Record on Learning: 'Only one who can explain by many metaphors is fit to be a teacher': basis for the Multi-metaphor (Boyu) pillar and the Field-Pairing Ground test scenario. Classical quotation only, not a planning basis.
Zhang Hua's 'Records of the Investigation of Things' (Bowu Zhi, Jin Dynasty): source of the Chinese master name 'Jing-Zhang Bowu Zhi'. Classical reference only.
Han Yu's 'On the Way' ('broad love is called benevolence'): basis for the Benevolence (Boai) pillar. Classical quotation only, not a planning basis.
Su Shi's 'Letter on Sending Zhang Hu off to Farm' ('observe broadly, extract selectively'): note to the visual style. Classical quotation only.
Ban Gu's History of the Han, Biography of the Prince of Chuyuan ('erudite and well-informed'): supporting classical reference for the master concept. Classical quotation only.
The Zuo Commentary, Duke Zhao 1st year ('a man of broad learning and noble character'): supporting classical reference for the master concept. Classical quotation only.
